{
  "per_column": [
    {
      "name": "crew_service_quality",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.9,
      "source_groundedness": 0.5,
      "hallucination_observed": true,
      "rationale": "Crew service is arguably the strongest driver of SIA ratings/recommendations, and a 4-way qualitative categorisation (warm/professional/robotic/rude) gives a genuine grouping axis beyond the raw Staff Service score. However groundedness is a real problem: in the seats-dreadful review (sample 2) the source text mentions nothing about crew, yet the value is 'rude_dismissive' — an invented negative. The near-even warm(3207)/rude(3073) split hints at systematic over-assignment of 'rude_dismissive' to negative reviews regardless of crew mention."
    },
    {
      "name": "food_quality_issue",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.85,
      "source_groundedness": 0.9,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Categorises food into actionable failure modes (taste, quantity, special-meal) rather than just echoing the numeric Food & Beverages score, so it adds leverage for identifying improvement levers. Samples are well grounded: praise mapped to 'praised_or_acceptable', and reviews silent on food correctly returned 'Unknown' rather than fabricating a category."
    },
    {
      "name": "seat_comfort_issue",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.8,
      "source_groundedness": 0.88,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Partially overlaps the existing numeric Seat Comfort column, but the issue-type breakdown (narrow/outdated/broken) is more actionable for targeting fixes, so it is not trivially redundant. Grounded in samples: 'seat far too narrow' → narrow_or_insufficient_legroom, comfortable seats → comfortable_no_issue, silence handled sensibly."
    },
    {
      "name": "disruption_handling_quality",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.85,
      "source_groundedness": 0.85,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Disruption handling is a plausible major driver of non-recommendation, so isolating it is a useful new axis. All sample reviews lack disruptions and are correctly marked 'not_applicable' — appropriate silent handling; no evidence of fabrication."
    },
    {
      "name": "customer_service_resolution_quality",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.85,
      "source_groundedness": 0.85,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Captures post-flight/complaint resolution, distinct from inflight service, giving a separate improvement dimension relevant to detractors. Samples that never contacted service are correctly 'not_contacted' rather than invented outcomes."
    },
    {
      "name": "ground_service_quality",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.8,
      "source_groundedness": 0.82,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Check-in/boarding/lounge is a genuine axis absent from the original numeric ratings, useful for locating friction outside the cabin. Samples with no ground-service mention are marked 'no_issue', a defensible default though slightly optimistic; no clear contradictions observed."
    },
    {
      "name": "ife_quality",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.75,
      "source_groundedness": 0.68,
      "hallucination_observed": true,
      "rationale": "Adds an issue-type view over the existing Inflight Entertainment numeric column. Groundedness is mixed: sample 2's 'sound...dreadful' fits a technical fault more than 'limited_or_outdated', and sample 4's review never mentions IFE yet was tagged 'excellent_or_adequate' — an over-confident positive where the text is silent. Positive/silent cases are otherwise handled reasonably."
    },
    {
      "name": "cabin_class_experience_gap",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.75,
      "source_groundedness": 0.7,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "The gap between class paid for and experience delivered is a valuable lens for premium-cabin improvement. It is fairly inferential, though: it requires combining Class with sentiment, and sample 2 (a very negative economy review) mapped to 'meets_class_expectations' is debatable. No outright invented facts, but values lean interpretive."
    },
    {
      "name": "service_decline_perception",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.6,
      "source_groundedness": 0.75,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "A bare boolean flag that is narrower than the qualitative columns and risks being close to a sentiment marker, so leverage is modest, though 'perceived decline vs past SIA' is a distinct brand-narrative angle. Samples with no temporal comparison correctly return 'false' rather than asserting a decline."
    },
    {
      "name": "service_consistency_across_legs",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.75,
      "source_groundedness": 0.82,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Useful for pinpointing where multi-leg journeys break down and separating one-off from systemic issues. Single-route reviews are correctly labelled 'single_leg' in every sample, showing appropriate restraint rather than fabricating leg-level variation."
    }
  ],
  "analytical_usefulness": 0.82,
  "source_groundedness": 0.72,
  "rationale": "The added columns form a coherent decomposition of free-text reviews into actionable service dimensions (crew, food, seat, IFE, ground, disruption, complaint resolution, class-gap, consistency, decline) that map directly onto levers SIA could pull to lift ratings and recommendation, and they enable grouping/comparison of non-recommending reviews by failure type — genuinely useful for this query, with only mild redundancy against the existing numeric sub-scores. Groundedness is generally solid, and silent rows are appropriately handled with 'Unknown'/'not_applicable' rather than fabrication. The main weaknesses are crew_service_quality (a clear 'rude_dismissive' assignment on a review that never mentions crew, plus a suspiciously high rude share suggesting systematic over-negativity) and ife_quality (asserting IFE quality where the text is silent), which pull the table-level groundedness down."
}
